source.title: Scalable Parameter and Memory Efficient Pretraining for LLM: Recent Algorithmic Advances and Benchmarking
source.authors: Athanasios Glentis; Jia-Xiang Li; Qiu-Lin Shang; Andi Han; Ioannis C. Tsaknakis; Quan Wei; Mingyi Hong

record.tranche_reason: The study measures evaluation perplexity against training compute for LLaMA pretraining runs and reports whether scaling-law-like behavior appears, using its own benchmark setup.
record.gate_note: Figure 5 and its discussion directly report evaluation perplexity versus FLOPs. Other benchmark results, including Table 3 comparisons of methods at fixed model sizes, memory estimates, and the momentum-reset/refactorization ablations, do not test the listed scaling-law versions and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 5 plots evaluation perplexity against training FLOPs on log-log axes for LLaMA 60M–1B pretraining on C4. It does this for full-rank, low-rank, LoRA and SLTrain methods and reports fitted slopes. This is a compute-scaling result in a new setting: parameter- and memory-efficient pretraining methods. It is not a replication of the originals' method: the curves pool all training trajectories across hyperparameter settings and fit perplexity rather than loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say all methods' perplexity scales inversely with FLOPs on log-log axes. Memory-efficient optimizers on full-rank models scale with very different slopes, with GaLore less efficient. The four weight-structure categories scale with similar slopes, so final perplexity depends mainly on FLOPs rather than model structure. The scaling result is a side analysis; the paper's main conclusions concern benchmarking efficient pretraining methods and the two proposed techniques.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LLaMA models from 60M to 1B, C4 without data repetition, and compute-perplexity trajectories across multiple pretraining methods; it is not a direct replication of the original scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling slope differs among full-rank memory-efficient optimizers; GaLore appears to scale less efficiently than the others. The four reported model-structure categories are said to have similar slopes.

fits_no_version.finding: Full-rank, low-rank, LoRA and SLTrain have similar perplexity–FLOPs slopes. The authors say final perplexity depends mainly on FLOPs and little on whether weights are full- or low-rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The compute-scaling exponent is largely invariant to weight parameterization (full-rank versus low-rank/sparse factorizations) in LM pretraining.

record.problems: The scaling result is reported for LLaMA models from 60M to 1B on C4 and does not isolate parameter count, token count, and compute. The paper does not report uncertainty for the scaling curves, per-run numeric results in the text, or a small-run-to-large-run prediction test. The authors also state that they did not conduct a comprehensive hyperparameter search for the 1B model.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling results bearing on the tested version were reported separately in text; Figure 5 scaling trajectories are recorded as the aggregate method-level results described by the authors.

untested.parts: Separate scaling in parameters or tokens with the others non-bottlenecking. A loss (not perplexity) power law. Compute-efficient frontier rather than pooled training trajectories. Range is only about 60M–1B parameters.
No extrapolation from small-run fits to larger runs.
No depth/width comparison at a fixed parameter count.
Text pretraining only; no other modalities, repeated data or fine-tuning scaling.
No test of parameter counting, schedule, data or fitting-method choices, and no curvature away from a power law. Only the optimizer-dependence of the slope is shown, and only from a figure.

missing.what: Final validation perplexity versus model size with tokens scaled jointly (about 20–27 tokens per parameter): full-rank Stable-SPAM 28.77, 22.20, 16.80 and 13.97 at 58M, 134M, 368M and 1339M parameters (1.4B–13.1B tokens); other methods are also listed. This is a joint N/D scaling series a researcher could fit.
Slope label -0.13 for the full-rank panel.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 5 pools training trajectories from all hyperparameter settings, using FLOPs = 6NBS, rather than a compute-efficient frontier. The fit is on perplexity on log-log axes. A power law in perplexity is not a power law in loss, though the two are hard to distinguish over this range. The 1B model had no full hyperparameter search. There is no uncertainty and no fit quality. Tranche changed from T2 to T3: this is a new setting (efficient pretraining methods), not a different method aimed at the original question.

versions.untested_parts: Tests the compute relationship using evaluation perplexity; does not separately vary parameter count or tokens while holding the other quantities non-bottlenecking, or establish the claim across all such settings.
No small-run fit is used to predict loss on substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget search for a loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is reported.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling experiment.
No downstream task performance is measured against scale or pretraining loss.

The paper reports differing scaling slopes across some training methods, but does not test sensitivity to fitting choices, disagreement between published scaling laws, or bending away from a single power law.

rows.subject: Full-rank LLaMA models
rows.size_stated: 60M, 130M, 350M, and 1B model sizes are included in the benchmark; scaling trajectories use different model sizes and training settings.
rows.operation_detail: Plots evaluation perplexity against training FLOPs across training trajectories.
rows.note: The authors state that the methods scale inversely with compute and that full-rank memory-efficient optimizers have substantially different slopes. This is an aggregate result across plotted trajectories; no per-model numeric values are given in the text.
rows.check: Fig 5(a) shows a slope label of -0.13 for full-rank, but the value records 'figure only'. The plot pools AdamW, Stable-SPAM, SPAM, GaLore and Fira, and the authors say their slopes differ 'very differently', so the row also bears on V7 (exponent depends on optimizer). For V1, the measure is perplexity (exp of loss) over within-run trajectories across hyperparameter settings, not a loss envelope.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1 benchmark metrics; Section 3.2 scaling paragraph; Figure 5(a).
source_check.problem: The observed state is justified for V7, but the perplexity scaling measure cannot establish V1's power-law loss.
